push_channel_down.title: Real-time push updates are not being received
push_channel_down.description:
The real-time push connection to RainPoint has been down for a while, so changes from your devices may be delayed.

Your devices keep updating regardless: polling every couple of minutes is still running as a fallback.

If this keeps happening, try one of:

- Reload the integration.
- Turn push updates off and back on in the integration's options.

push_hub_identity_unresolved.title: Push updates could not start
push_hub_identity_unresolved.description:
Push updates are turned on, but the integration could not find a usable hub to connect to, so real-time updates are not arriving.

Your devices keep updating regardless: polling every couple of minutes is still running as a fallback.

This check only runs when the integration reloads (options change, restart, or a manual reload), so a fix will not clear this notice on its own until then.

If this keeps happening, try one of:

- Reload the integration.
- Turn push updates off and back on in the integration's options.

hub_disconnected.title: A hub is not reachable from the RainPoint service
hub_disconnected.description:
RainPoint has reported **{hub_name}** ({model}) as offline, and it has stayed that way for at least {offline_for}. A brief drop does not raise this notice, so this is a sustained outage rather than a blip.

This usually means the hub is unplugged, has lost its network connection, or your home network itself is down.

Readings from devices paired to this hub keep showing their last known values while it is offline: RainPoint keeps serving the last reading it received rather than reporting nothing, so a reading that looks current may not be. Valve controls for those devices are also unavailable while the hub is offline, since a command cannot reach hardware the cloud cannot talk to.

This notice clears on its own after the hub reconnects, and its devices catch up at the same time. With push updates enabled it clears within seconds; otherwise it waits for the next scheduled check, so allow up to two minutes. For the live signal, check the hub's own **Cloud Connection** entity, which carries the current state and its history.

init.title: RainPoint Options
init.description: Polling is always retained as a fallback.

data.generic_control_enabled: Enable unverified generic device control (moves hardware)
data.hic_control_probe_enabled: Run the irrigation controller command test (writes to the controller)

data_description.push_enabled: Receive real-time updates from the RainPoint cloud instead of waiting for the next poll. Polling is always retained as a fallback. Push is on by default; uncheck this to turn it off.
data_description.generic_entities_enabled:
Adds provisional sensors for devices this integration does not support yet. These readings are derived from RainPoint's product catalog rather than a tested per-model decoder, so they may be wrong. They are always labeled unverified in their names and should not be relied on for automations.

Generic sensors are only created for a device once every reading it reports has a verified definition, so many devices produce none at all. On this account that currently applies to {generic_eligible} of {generic_unsupported} unsupported devices. This option is off by default.
data_description.generic_control_enabled:
Adds controls that open and close real hardware -- including water valves -- for devices this integration does not support yet. The zone mapping comes from RainPoint's product catalog rather than a tested per-model decoder, so a wrong mapping can run the wrong zone or leave water running.

Nothing is assumed about the outcome of a command: a control entity only ever shows state read back from the device, never a guess. On this account that currently applies to {generic_control_eligible} of {generic_control_unsupported} unsupported devices. This option is off by default.
data_description.hic_control_probe_enabled:
Only turn this on if you have been asked to, in a support thread about your irrigation controller. It adds two test buttons to the controller's device page and nothing else changes.

Home Assistant can read this controller but cannot yet start or stop a station, because the controller never reports back how that command is worded and no amount of further readings can reveal it. These buttons work it out by trying the possibilities and watching which one the controller acts on.

The first button sets a rain delay. That waters nothing whatever happens, so it is safe to press at any time; check the RainPoint app afterwards to see whether a rain delay appeared. The second button tries to start one station for one minute and then stops it again. Turn the water off at the tap or backflow before pressing that one: the controller still reports what it did with the water off, so nothing is lost by being careful.

After pressing, download the diagnostics from this integration's page and attach the file to the thread. This option is off by default.
